verdict.rationale: cubic's own docs cover both halves of the story. The CLI generates a prompt your coding agent can use to fix findings, and an official MCP server lets coding agents read review findings and triage issues. Setup is documented for Cursor, Claude Code, Codex and other tools, and skills are provided for handling PR comments. Missing for 10: no independent or hands-on corroboration of the agent handoff working in practice; copyable fix prompts are documented only for local CLI reviews, not for PR review comments.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, review findings hand off cleanly to my coding agent — copyable fix prompts or direct integration with Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex

citations.quote: It finds bugs and generates a prompt that your coding agent can use to fix them.
Connect cubic's MCP server to your coding agent to read review findings and codebase context, request PR reviews, and triage PR or codebase scan issues.
Install and connect cubic in Cursor, Claude Code, VS Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, or another coding tool.
cubic skills give your coding agent instructions for reviewing code, handling PR comments, and using your team's codebase context.
